title: Kanau Lite
description: A free app that turns an iPhone or iPad into one light, controlled over Art-Net or sACN. Getting started, modes and channels, FX & MEDIA, COOKIE and ULTIMATE, patching on a desk.
body:
Kanau Lite is a free app that turns an iPhone or iPad into one light. It receives DMX sent from a desk over Art-Net or sACN, and drives the color and brightness of the screen, the back light and the vibration. In the FX & MEDIA and ULTIMATE modes, the screen can also show moving patterns and your own images and videos. There is no account to create and there are no ads.

What you need

  • An iPhone or iPad on iOS 17 or later.
  • A desk that sends Art-Net or sACN. Kanau or any other desk.
  • The same network as the desk, over Wi-Fi or a wired connection. The first time you open the app, it asks for Local Network access. Allow it.

Getting started

  1. Open Kanau Lite. The icon and the name show for a moment. Tap to skip them.
  2. Settings opens. It comes first each time Kanau Lite opens.
  3. Choose Art-Net or sACN. Then set Mode, Universe and Address.
  4. Tap START at the bottom.
  5. From the desk, send DMX to that universe and address. When it arrives, the screen becomes the light.

Until you tap START, the screen does not light up, even if DMX arrives.

The address screen

After START, while no DMX is arriving, a black screen shows three lines in large type. This is the address screen. With many devices side by side, you can read each number from a distance.

  • The universe and address, in amber, for example U1 · 001.
  • The mode, for example SCREEN RGB 10ch.
  • The network, this device's IP address and the protocol it listens for, for example Wi-Fi 192.168.1.24 · Art-Net. With no network, it shows No network.

Tap the address screen to open Settings. If no DMX arrives for 6 seconds while the light is on, the address screen comes back. The back light and the vibration stop too.

Settings

From the top:

ItemWhat it does
LanguageSystem, or one of 15 languages. The explanations change as soon as you choose. Names of items and buttons stay in English. Until you choose, Kanau Lite is in English.
GuideOpens a short guide in 8 steps. It is inside the app, so it works without the internet.
Art-Net / sACNTap one of the two. The one you choose turns amber.
ModeShows the current mode, for example SCREEN RGB 10ch. Tap it to choose from the modes below (see Modes and channels). On a device without a back light, BACK LIGHT ONLY is not listed.
Universe0–32767 for Art-Net, 1–63999 for sACN.
AddressFrom 1 up to the highest address that still fits the mode's channels within 512.
MediaShows how many of the 51 numbers hold an image or a video, for example 3 / 51. Tap it to open the shelf (see Media).

Type a number for Universe and Address, or use − and +. The amber line below them shows the addresses used by the screen, the back light and the vibration, for example Screen 001–008 · Back Light 009 · Vibration 010.

Next is Channels. Each time you open Settings, it starts folded and shows only the number of channels, for example 10ch. Tap the heading to open the list of the current mode's channels, with their address, name and what the values mean. The two lines on patching on Kanau and on other desks show even while it is folded. A row for a feature this device does not have (the back light or the vibration) is dimmed and starts with Not on this device. That row still uses its address, so count it on the desk too.

At the end of Settings are the Kanau Lite version, Made by Kanau Labs, a link to kanaulabs.app, Privacy Policy, Contact Support, the Art-Net credit and the copyright. Settings are saved and are still there the next time you open the app.

While the light is on

The screen shows what it receives. While Kanau Lite is open, the screen stays at full brightness and does not lock automatically.

To open Settings while the light is on, slide the faint switch at the top right all the way to the right, then tap the × that appears. The × goes away after 3 seconds. Settings opened this way closes with × at the top left.

Kanau Lite receives DMX only while the app is open. If you go to the Home Screen or lock the device, it stops receiving, stops the back light and the vibration, and sets the screen brightness back to what it was. Open it again to receive again.

Modes and channels

There are 19 modes. The default is SCREEN RGB 10ch.

ModeScreen
BACK LIGHT ONLY 1chUses the back light only. The screen stays dark.
SCREEN RGB 10ch
SCREEN HUE SAT 9ch		The whole screen is one color.
SCREEN 2 CELLS RGB 18ch
SCREEN 2 CELLS HUE SAT 16ch		The screen is split into 2.
SCREEN 4 CELLS RGB 32ch
SCREEN 4 CELLS HUE SAT 28ch		The screen is split into 4.
SCREEN 8 CELLS RGB 60ch
SCREEN 8 CELLS HUE SAT 52ch		The screen is split into 8.
SCREEN 4 STRIPS RGB 32ch
SCREEN 4 STRIPS HUE SAT 28ch		The screen is split into 4 strips along its long side.
SCREEN 8 STRIPS RGB 60ch
SCREEN 8 STRIPS HUE SAT 52ch		The screen is split into 8 strips along its long side.
SCREEN FX & MEDIA RGB 19ch
SCREEN FX & MEDIA HUE SAT 18ch		The whole screen, with patterns, images and videos (see FX & MEDIA).
SCREEN COOKIE RGB 63ch
SCREEN COOKIE HUE SAT 55ch		The screen is split into irregular, dappled areas in 8 colors (see COOKIE and ULTIMATE).
ULTIMATE RGB 73ch
ULTIMATE HUE SAT 65ch		Chooses how to split the screen, and shows patterns, images and videos (see COOKIE and ULTIMATE).

Apart from BACK LIGHT ONLY, every mode starts with Screen Dimmer and ends with Function, Back Light and Vibration. SCREEN RGB 10ch has these channels, in this order. The values are written as they appear in Channels in Settings.

#NameValues
1Screen Dimmer0–100%
2CCT1,750–9,910 K · Home 117 = 5,494 K
3G/M0–4 No effect · 5 Magenta → 255 Green · Home 128
4Crossfade0 White → 255 Color · Home 0
5Red0–100%
6Green0–100%
7Blue0–100%
8Function0–127 Off · 128–255 Proximity · Home 0
9Back Light0–100%
10Vibration0–100%

The HUE SAT modes have Hue (0–360°) and Saturation instead of Red, Green and Blue. In the CELLS and STRIPS modes, Screen Dimmer is followed by Dimmer, CCT, G/M, Crossfade and the color for each part of the screen. CELLS are numbered from the top left. With 8 cells, a portrait screen has 2 columns and 4 rows, and a landscape screen has 4 columns and 2 rows. STRIPS are strips of equal width placed along the long side of the screen. A portrait screen has horizontal strips numbered from top to bottom, and a landscape screen has vertical strips numbered from left to right. A square screen is split from top to bottom.

Crossfade sets the mix of white and color: 0 is white and 255 is color. The white comes from CCT and G/M. While Crossfade is at 0, raising Red, Green or Blue leaves the screen white. Screen Dimmer dims the screen only and does not affect the back light. Setting Function to 128 or higher selects Proximity, which uses the device's proximity sensor.

FX & MEDIA

SCREEN FX & MEDIA RGB 19ch has these channels, in this order. SCREEN FX & MEDIA HUE SAT 18ch has Hue and Saturation instead of Red, Green and Blue.

#NameValues
1Screen Dimmer0–100%
2CCT1,750–9,910 K · Home 117 = 5,494 K
3G/M0–4 No effect · 5 Magenta → 255 Green · Home 128
4Crossfade0 White → 255 Color · Home 0
5Red0–100%
6Green0–100%
7Blue0–100%
8Color Macro0–15 Off · 16–255 15 colors, 16 each · Home 0
9Content0 SOLID · 32 GLINT · 64 SWEEP · 96 KALEIDO · 128 WATER · 160 FIRE · 192 VIDEO GLOW · 224 CATCHLIGHT · Home 0
10Speed0 Slow · 128 Normal · 255 Fast · Home 128
11Amount0–255 · Home 128
12Size0–255 · Home 128
13Mix0 Media → 255 Pattern · Home 255
14Media0 Off · 1–5 = 1 · 6–10 = 2 … 251–255 = 51 · Home 0
15Playback0–85 Play · 86–170 Pause · 171–255 Restart · Home 0
16Color Temp0 Warm · 128 As is · 255 Cool · Home 128
17Function0–127 Off · 128–255 Proximity · Home 0
18Back Light0–100%
19Vibration0–100%

The screen is built up from black: first the image or video chosen by Media, then the pattern chosen by Content on top of it. Mix sets how much of each you see: 0 shows only the image or video, and 255 shows only the pattern. When Media is 0, or the number holds nothing, only the pattern shows.

SOLID, the first Content, fills the screen with the color. At the Home values, FX & MEDIA gives the same light as SCREEN RGB. The other seven are patterns that move. Speed sets how fast they move, and Amount and Size change how each pattern looks. A pattern takes its color from the screen's color. When Color Macro is not 0, the macro color is used instead. From 16, each 16 values pick the next color: 3200 K, 4300 K, 5600 K, Red, Orange, Amber, Yellow, Green, Cyan, Sky Blue, Blue, Deep Blue, Lavender, Magenta and Pink.

Images and videos keep their own colors. Color Temp shifts them warmer or cooler, and Screen Dimmer dims them. Videos play without sound and start again from the beginning when they end. Playback plays or pauses the video. Restart sends it back to the beginning once, at the moment the value enters 171–255.

COOKIE and ULTIMATE

SCREEN COOKIE splits the screen into irregular, dappled areas. Each area has the color of one of the 8 cells, so the color of one cell shows in several places on the screen. For light and shadow, set some of the cells to black on the desk.

SCREEN COOKIE RGB 63ch starts with Screen Dimmer, then Shape, Soft and Drift. Next come the 8 cells, each with Dimmer, CCT, G/M, Crossfade, Red, Green and Blue, as in the CELLS modes. Function, Back Light and Vibration come last. SCREEN COOKIE HUE SAT 55ch has Hue and Saturation in each cell instead of Red, Green and Blue.

#NameValues
2Shape0–255 Pattern · Home 0
3Soft0 Sharp → 255 Soft · Home 0
4Drift0 Still → 255 Fast · Home 0

Shape chooses the pattern. The pattern changes smoothly as the value moves, so a fade on the desk turns one pattern into the next. Soft blurs the edges between the areas: at 0 they are sharp. Drift sets how fast the pattern flows: at 0 it stands still.

ULTIMATE RGB 73ch has the channels of COOKIE, FX & MEDIA and 8 cells, in this order.

#NameValues
1Screen Dimmer0–100%
2Cells0 SCREEN · 32 2 CELLS · 64 4 CELLS · 96 8 CELLS · 128 4 STRIPS · 160 8 STRIPS · 192 COOKIE · Home 0
3–5Shape, Soft, DriftAs in COOKIE
6–14Color Macro, Content, Speed, Amount, Size, Mix, Media, Playback, Color TempAs in FX & MEDIA
15–70Dimmer 1 … Blue 87 channels for each cell, as in the CELLS modes
71–73Function, Back Light, VibrationAs in the other modes

ULTIMATE HUE SAT 65ch has 6 channels for each cell, with Hue and Saturation, so the cells are 15–62 and Function, Back Light and Vibration are 63–65.

The cells show only while Content is SOLID and Media is 0. Cells then chooses how the screen is split. SCREEN fills the whole screen with the color of cell 1. While a pattern, an image or a video shows (Content is not SOLID, or Media is not 0), the screen is one, as in FX & MEDIA, and the pattern takes the color of cell 1. Media counts by its value: a value other than 0 makes the screen one, even if that number holds nothing. Color Macro works only while the screen is one. While the screen is split, it has no effect. When Cells splits the screen into fewer than 8 parts, the channels of the other cells have no effect, but still use their addresses.

Media

The shelf holds images and videos on this device under the numbers 1 to 51. Open it from Media in Settings. It is there in every mode, so you can fill it before you switch to FX & MEDIA or ULTIMATE.

  • Tap an empty number to add an image or a video from Photos or from Files.
  • Tap a number in use to replace what it holds, move it to another number, or delete it. If the other number is in use, the two swap.

On the desk, the Media channel picks the number: 1–5 is 1, 6–10 is 2, and so on, up to 251–255 for 51. The files stay on this device and are not sent anywhere.

Patching on a desk

On Kanau, patch this device as Kanau Screen with the same mode (chapter 03 of the manual). In Kanau 1.0 (371), Kanau Screen has all 19 modes.

On other desks, make a fixture with the channels in the same order as Channels in Settings, and patch it at the same address. Every channel is 8-bit.

Over Art-Net, the app answers node discovery (ArtPoll) with a name such as Kanau Screen · U1 · 001. On a desk that can list nodes, look for this name, with its universe and address.

How it differs from LITE MODE in Kanau

Kanau Lite receives the same way as LITE MODE in Kanau (chapter 02 of the manual). As of Kanau 1.0 (371), four things are different.

  • Before DMX arrives, LITE MODE shows WAITING. Kanau Lite shows the address screen.
  • When DMX stops, LITE MODE keeps the last color. Kanau Lite goes back to the address screen after 6 seconds.
  • The × from the top-right switch leaves LITE MODE in Kanau. In Kanau Lite, it opens Settings.
  • The Media shelf is only in Kanau Lite. In LITE MODE, the FX & MEDIA and ULTIMATE modes show patterns only.

Contact

Write to info@kanaulabs.app in any language, or use Contact Support in Settings. For a bug report, please include the Kanau Lite version shown at the end of Settings, the mode you used, and your desk and protocol.
